# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

11	> **Design Review (first formal, 2026-10-27)**: the 7 BLOCKING findings are fixed (cell-unit occlusion convention, FAULT_GLOW anchor, `supported_versions`, `run_pm`-only lanterns, probes deferred to VS-A, synchronous rebuild contract with priced scenarios, sim-side strobe guard) and the RECOMMENDED set is applied or routed; every edited paragraph and row carries "*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*". Decisions that only the user can make were Open Questions marked **USER DECISION** (rows 1–4, 17, 23; all ruled below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **User rulings (design-review decisions), 2026-10-27:** rows 1–4 (D20–D23) kept as written, row 17 (D24) adopts `BEAM_SPILL_RADIUS_PX` 24 as the shipped default with a conditional `light_shape` row 11, and the dock-room status glow (X2) adds a second self-powered fixture subkind; the deliberately shape-blind light stimulus (row 23, D25) and the sim-side switch commit spacing `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (D32, rows 25 and 29) are defaults applied pending the user's confirmation. The reference machine for the exposure benchmark (row 28, X14) stays OPEN. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
12	> **Re-review (2026-10-27, delegated rulings: the user said "just use best judgment")**: the five BLOCKING findings are fixed (the new-game lamp now arms and carries its 20 W request at E1, with the DOCK_STATUS glow switched by a new mutator E10 instead of by `pod_at` read at E1; AC-12e uses `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`; AC-52 carries a Result column and honest I-CAPS arithmetic; AC-52e iterates only the REFUSE rows; the word "live" no longer names two sets, and AC-33 and AC-67 have one row per node state). The RECOMMENDED set is applied, with the D.14 repricing, the spill read-view accessor, the evict-wane floor form, the I-DOCK / I-SPACING / I-WANE corrections, the testability rewrites and the `lit_static` deferral. The ON-then-OFF spacing (D32) stays a default pending confirmation, now with its `12 − L` table and options (Open Question 31). Every edited paragraph and row carries "*(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*". *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
13	
14	## Summary
15	
16	Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query is the headless, integer-only simulation record of every light in the world (the chest beam, ship fixtures, machinery lanterns, thrown glowsticks, alarm beacons and fault glows) plus the one question it answers: how much of that light reaches a registered point, and is it enough to work by. Read this GDD if you design or build anything that must ask "is this lit" (Interaction's lit-only verbs, Attention's light stimulus, Horror Entities, Suit's beam charge, 2D Lighting's drawn edge, Derelict Authoring's lamps): it fixes the emitter records and their commands and mutators, the shape table, the lamp, glowstick, beacon and fault-glow formulas, the cone and occlusion tests, the hysteresis, the caps and the acceptance criteria, and it never reads a `Light2D`, a physics space or a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view.
17	
18	**Two `lit`s, kept verbatim (EM-2):** the *record field* `emitter.state.lit` means an emitter is emitting (`output_pm > 0`, true for any kind and read by the Presenter on the seat's beam); the *query* `lit(ref)` means a registered subject's exposure is above the technical-artist's threshold with hysteresis (`LIT_ON_PM` 150 / `LIT_OFF_PM` 120). Neither is ever renamed.
19	
20	> **Quick reference** — Layer: `Feature` (systems-index enumeration row 5, Recommended Design Order 7; Category Core) · Priority: `MVP` · Key deps: `Command & Simulation Layer`, `Life-Support Graph`, `Player Controller & Input`, Layout, Item & Module Database, Suit & Equipment, Ship Body (all designed; the counterparts that were undesigned at first draft — Layout, Suit, Ship Body, Interaction, 2D Lighting, Attention, Horror, Derelict Authoring — are now Status Designed, so the contracts below are two-sided and an item still tagged provisional waits on a counterpart's text, not on a missing GDD) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Depended on by 6 systems on the index's graph (2D Lighting & Occlusion, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Derelict Authoring, Attention, Horror Entities), and read without an index edge by Web Map & Transit (hard: E1 at `init_world`, E10, `lit` for the pod console), Failure & Trail, Adaptive Audio & Tells and the HUD & Suit Layer (soft; Open Question 15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.
21	
22	## Overview
23	
24	Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query is the simulation's record of every light in the world and the one question it answers about them: *how much of that light reaches this point, and is it enough to work by?* In one sentence: it is a scene-tree-free, integer-only `SIM` block, `emitter.state`, that holds an **emitter record** for each chest beam, ship fixture, machinery lantern, thrown glowstick, alarm beacon and fault glow, written only through commands and published mutators, plus a pure **exposure query** that combines those records with the Layout's opaque footprints into a per-subject `lux_pm` (0..1000) and a `lit` bit. It is the data layer under three things the player feels directly: the edge of their own lamp (what the lamp reaches is exactly what they can read and touch), the dimming of a ship lamp when the scrubber draws, and the way the web answers to light (Attention, Horror Entities and the act-only-on-lit rule all read the same answers). It never reads a `Light2D`, never touches a physics space, never obtains a `PERCEPTION_OUT` view, and runs identically headless, on the host and under test.
25	
26	The player never operates an emitter table. They meet it as a **pool of light with an edge**. The chest lamp (hands-free, Pandorum-style, origin at the per-facing chest point, `|x| <= 2` px) lays a wedge across the deck; a valve wheel half inside it prompts exactly when the wheel's anchor crosses the drawn edge and not a pixel sooner; the corridor lamps sag when the tier browns out and the junction box at the rim of their pool loses its prompt; a glowstick thrown into the next room blooms Chemlight green, holds steady, and then visibly shrinks; a lamp switched on takes a handful of ticks to warm because the ship has to serve it first. Nothing is ever shown as an exposure readout of any shape, or a "visibility" number (P3: shown in the world, never as a hidden meter): the only gameplay surface of the whole system is a prompt that is present or absent, drawn by the HUD, and the world itself.
27	
28	The block exists because three decisions already made elsewhere need one honest place to live. The index (TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY) split *emitter state* from *light rendering* so that light is a simulation input no hallucination can touch (kernel CR-12) and so that Attention can run headless and on the host for remote players. The Controller made the beam an emitter "like any other for Attention" and made every verb act only on a lit object (PC-5, PC-6), which demands one query that the prompt, the `validate` step and the channel re-check all call. The Graph made lamps ordinary LOADs whose brightness is `base * served_pm / 1000` (registry formula `power_allocation`), which demands a place that turns that served power into a light a subject can be inside of. The result is a bottleneck with six dependents (2D Lighting & Occlusion, Interaction, Suit & Equipment, Derelict Authoring, Attention, Horror Entities).
29	
30	**What the game loses without it.** There is no honest "go dark" strategy (nothing for Attention to read), no lit-only rule (PC-6 has no query to call), no way for a lamp to be dimmer because the ship is starved (P1: "a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served"), no stable edge for the Tell's filaments to resolve at (P2), and no sim-side truth for Lighting to conform to, so the first hallucination that bends a cone would be indistinguishable from a bug. The sim/render agreement that this block guarantees by construction (the drawn hard edge *is* the queried edge for a full-output emitter) is the load-bearing P1 test of the whole lighting stack.
31	
32	**Index wording, reconciled.** The index (rationale bullet 5) describes a geometric light-exposure query made of a cone test plus occluder tests on physics shapes. This GDD honours the substance, the Layout's collision footprint rectangles as the occluding shapes, and changes the means: occlusion is an integer segment-versus-rectangle test against those same rectangles behind an `OccluderSource` seam, with no physics backend in the MVP (EM-20). The reason is the index's own intent — the block "runs headless" and lets Attention run headless and on the host (kernel H10; CR-13 G3: the 2D physics engine makes no determinism claim, so a physics-derived `lit` flowing into a persisted block would have to be recorded for replay). The index and kernel wording refresh this implies is routed in Cross-References. Index numbering, once and for all: this system is **enumeration row 5**, rationale bullet 5, **Recommended Design Order 7**.
33	
34	*Implementation questions raised while designing and deferred to ADRs (→ `/architecture-decision`): the `OccluderSource` seam and the integer segment test (ADR candidate 1); the subject-registration model with static and dynamic layers and counted work units (ADR candidate 2); the fixed-point direction table and Q28 cone test with zero floats on the sim path (ADR candidate 3); the broadphase (uniform grid versus room-gated) and whether the spatial index lives in Layout or here (ADR candidate 4); the occlusion-origin rule, contingent on the Lighting spike (ADR candidate 5). No ADR exists yet (`docs/architecture/` holds only `tr-registry.yaml`). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The review adds to candidate 1 the **cell convention** of D.6 (cells as unit squares, doubled coordinates), to candidate 4 the **static-rebuild policy** (D.14 scenarios; synchronous, with the per-pair cache and the narrowing of door-leaf invalidation) and the (b) alternative it rejects, and a new candidate 6, the **read-view storage layout** (EM-25: typed or packed columns, sorted subject columns, a per-tick snapshot). Under workflow tier `full` these six ADRs are written with `/architecture-decision` before story breakdown, and the inline rulings and "alternatives considered" text then move into them (Open Question 24).*
35	
36	## Player Fantasy
37	
38	**Framing: indirect, with a cost layer.** The player experiences this system as the edge of their own light and the prompts that live inside it; they never see "exposure", an "emitter" or a "query". *(creative-director consulted; Framing A "The Honest Edge" adopted as the headline, with Framing C "Light as a Spend" as its price. Framing B "Lamp Management" — brightness dials, shape switching, lamp banks as a resource panel — was rejected: it breeds an exposure readout, which P3 forbids, and a shape-change input, which PC-5 forbids. Logged.)*
39	
40	> The lamp is on your chest. It is the only light that follows you, and it is the only way to touch anything: what is not in the light cannot be worked (the four exceptions of the registry `act_gate` aside: `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument and `throw_glowstick`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Every fixture on the home-ship, every running machine's lantern, every glowstick you leave behind is the same bargain. Light lets you read the ship, and light lets the web read you.
41	>
42	> Competence is choosing light, not having more of it. A veteran crew does not carry a brighter lamp; they know which corridor lamp to kill before a sortie, where a glowstick buys the most room for the least time, and when a second of beam on a dark corner is worth what it shows.
43	>
44	> And the edge never lies. Eyes can be wrong about what stands in the light, but not about where the light ends. When the sanity goes, the dark may fill with shapes and the cone may seem to reach further than it does; walk to the edge and it is exactly where it always was, and nothing past it will answer your hand.
45	
46	**The emotion named: the bargain of sight** — agency purchased with exposure, under a guarantee that the light itself is never the liar. The power is not dominance over the dark; it is the small, honest sovereignty of your own light: you choose where the edge of the known world is, and the edge is where you left it.
47	
48	**Tone and language.** Use: *lamp, chest lamp, beam, in the light, the edge, go dark, the lamp warms, the pool shrinks, spend light.* Avoid meter words (*visibility, detection, stealth, hidden, light level, lux*; `lux_pm` is an internal name and is never player-facing) and avoid *flashlight* (it implies a hand-held tool; the lamp is chest-mounted) and *torch* for the beam (the anti-pillars use "torches" for the VS-A deployables; concept Pillar 1's "carries their torch" means the beam, a wording refresh owed to the concept, listed in Cross-References). The ludonarrative anchor is the user's decision of 2026-10-26: the lamp is on the player's chest, hands-free, like Pandorum. The player *is* the lantern, so going dark is not putting a tool down; it is hiding your own body.
49	
50	**Anchor moment (solo; the MVP is single-player).** Derelict A, power dead. The hatch opens on black. You thumb the chest lamp on: the click comes first, the light a breath later (PC-5: the sound pre-plays, the light follows committed state). A wedge of your wide beam — 30° half-angle, 288 px / 6 tiles, placeholder rows of the art bible 8.3 table — lays a hard edge across the deck plates. At the far end of it, half in, half out, a valve wheel. You turn a hair to the left and the wheel's prompt appears at the same moment the wheel does; a hair back and both are gone. The edge is a fact. The next compartment is past a bulkhead your beam cannot bend around. You crack a glowstick and throw it (Interaction's throw, `THROW_RANGE_TILES` 3). Chemlight green (#86B896) blooms in a room you have not entered yet, a 2-tile pool (96 px, an Item DB placeholder) that will not flicker but will shrink. Now there are two lights in this derelict and only one of them follows you. Something creaks overhead; filaments are resolving at the rim of your cone (Attention's presentation). You switch the lamp off. The dark is honest: the valve still exists, you just cannot touch it now. Behind you the glowstick you left keeps burning. You chose to leave it. It is still lit, and it is still yours to answer for.
51	
52	**Second beat (home-ship, Graph-coupled).** Back aboard, the scrubber spins up and the corridor lamps sag as the power tier browns out (`lamp_output_pm` = `base * served_pm / 1000`). The pool under the galley lamp pulls in; the junction box at the edge of it, which you could reach a minute ago, is now outside the light and has no prompt. Nobody told you the power is short. The light told you. *(The crewmate beats — a downed crewmate's beam as a locator in the dark, a saner crewmate's beam as the truth check — are Vertical Slice B (VS-B); the MVP fantasy rests on the honesty of your own edge.)*
53	
54	**Pillar alignment.** *Pillar 1 (primary), verbatim:* "Three channels are inviolable ... The human channel. Voice/proximity chat and a crewmate's own light beam (colour and shape) are never faked." And the art bible's Principle 1 anchor: "The physical radius your light actually reveals is a fixed anchor and never lies. Even at low sanity, the hallucination layer may add things but may not move that boundary." This block is that anchor in the simulation: the edge the player sees is the edge the query answers. *Pillar 3 (primary), verbatim:* "The players' light, noise, power use and restraint raise or lower its attention ... shown in the world, never as a hidden meter ... Restraint and stealth are real strategies." Every emitter is exposure; off-screen emitters still expose; going dark is a real, measured choice. *Pillar 4:* "No lie is unfalsifiable: the truth is always available through the physical world, a second instrument, a saner crewmate, the human channel, or time — and checking costs time, risk or trust." The true edge is a falsifier that costs a step and the exposure of standing in your own beam. *Pillar 2 (supporting):* the Tell's signature image, filaments resolving at the cone edge, needs a stable edge to resolve at. *Pillar 5 is not served* (glowstick scarcity is Suit's and the Item DB's). The "spend light" cost layer leans on glowstick scarcity, which is P5-adjacent (scarcity pushes inward), so the spend has a named economic owner and is not an unanchored promise: **the scarcity-to-depth link is routed to the Item & Module Database and Suit & Equipment** (the Item DB's `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` and its salvage-only faucet, Suit's per-seat carry and start counts, and Derelict Authoring's loose-stick supply by depth); this GDD prices the light (a stick is a real, shrinking reveal radius and a real exposure) and owns none of the supply.
55	
56	**Design tests.**
57	1. **The honest edge (system test).** *When the place you can act differs from the place you can see light vs. they coincide → they coincide.* At rest (aim committed, not sweeping), an object whose anchor is one base pixel inside the drawn hard edge of a single full-output hard-edged emitter is in the light and prompts; one pixel outside is not and does not. This is the sim/render agreement test (a `(spike)` until Lighting exists). It holds for a *full-output* emitter; a dimmed emitter's actionable area honestly shrinks (see Formulas, `EDGE_FLOOR_PM`).
58	2. **Light is the price of agency.** *When a choice lets the player act without light vs. requires light to act → require light.* (the registry `act_gate` exemptions, four: `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the inspect card of an already-lit instrument and `throw_glowstick`; the first draft listed three) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Otherwise working in the dark becomes a free Attention dodge and "go dark" degenerates into the dominant strategy.
59	3. **Light is never free.** *When a choice makes a light safe (unseen by the web, no cost) vs. keeps every emitter an exposure → exposure.* Corollary: off-screen emitters still expose; a glowstick you walked away from is still yours to answer for.
60	4. **The lie draws, it does not reach.** *When a hallucination could change what is actionable vs. only what is drawn → only what is drawn.* No Filter output changes `emitter.state` or any query answer.
61	
62	**Under hallucination the fantasy deepens rather than breaks.** Light gets the same split the Graph drew for the physical world. The left column is what this GDD guarantees by construction (a `SIM`-only block, kernel CR-12, EM-29); the right is what the Perception Filter and Lighting may do, as presentation only.
63	
64	| Cannot lie (truth channel — this GDD guarantees) | Can lie (presentation — a decoy overlay drawn by Lighting on mask bit 3 from the Filter's per-viewer decoy list, LO-21) |
65	|---|---|
66	| The true reveal edge of every emitter: reach, cone, occlusion | Decoy lights that are not emitters (not in `emitter.state`, expose nothing) |
67	| Beam colour and shape, including a crewmate's (VS-B) | Shadows with no occluder (stage-2 drift, art bible 4.4) |
68	| Lamp and fixture brightness as served (`lamp_output_pm`) | A decoy glow appears past the true edge (an overlay, leaking violet) |
69	| Whether an object is in the light (`lit(subject)`), and therefore whether it prompts and accepts verbs | A decoy overlay that may itself flicker, on the decoy mask bit (Lighting; flash-clamped) |
70	| Glowstick waning: a real, monotone shrinking of the reveal radius | What a lit object looks like (the module-body channel: sprite, gauge) |

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). - Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

The 8 GDD sections, in order:

3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where

before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.

103	## Detailed Design
104	
105	### Core Rules
106	
107	*Every rule below is a sim rule of the Emitter State owner module (`src/sim/emitter/`), stated so that an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Registry constants are cited by their registered name (`TICK_RATE` 60, `TILE_PX` 48, `AIM_UNITS` 4096, `REACH_PX` 72, `WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6, `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4, `rng_derive`, `state_hash`, `hook_runs_this_tick`, `chest_point`, `power_allocation`, `served_pm`, and the Graph's `INRUSH_STEPS` 5 / `INRUSH_PM` 1500) and are never restated with another value; owner-GDD tuning rows that are not registry entries (the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD`, `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS`, `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN`) are cited by name the same way. Every number this GDD introduces has its own name and the tag "placeholder, owner X, confirmed by Y" (Tuning Knobs); a number another GDD owns is cited by that GDD's name for it. Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it. The tool-grip anchor `HAND_POINT` is lightless and is never read by this block, and no rule anywhere names it an origin. The beam follows *aim*, not facing: facing diverges from aim while running (PC-4 rule 3). The drawn cone and the simulated cone may diverge by up to the PC-5 accepted tolerance (≤ 2.8°, ≤ 1 tick; the Controller's `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` / `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` knobs widen it to 3 ticks), which is why the agreement test (design test 1) is stated at rest. **Occlusion starts at the foot, not the chest** *(orchestrator ruling: the foot-origin rule of the technical-director over the systems-designer's sanitised walk-back, because `pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction — `LocomotionStep` keeps the avatar's box out of them — and is free of the 2 px mirror jitter; the walk-back remains the documented alternative, ADR candidate 5)*: `CHEST_POINT.y` is -45..-25 px (`h` = −y, 25..45), so with a 24 px wall footprint the chest point stands *inside* the footprint whenever the feet are `s` px south of the first legal row in front of a north wall (`s` = 0 on that row, LY-8 b) with `h − 24 ≤ s ≤ h − 1`: the band is **1–44 px** over all animation rows (10–33 px for the walk row at `h` 34 — the first draft's "10-34" was one row's band, not the range). 167	**EM-7 — The beam changes only on committed state.** `toggle_beam` is owned by Emitter State and fixed by the Controller (PC-5, PC-2): `actor` = the seat's beam emitter id, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, origin `PLAYER`. The payload carries no state (it is a toggle: the `beam_toggle` press flips `switch_on`), so a rejected or duplicated command can never desynchronise the intent. Its apply flips `switch_on` in P2 of tick T; `emitter.place` in P3 of the same tick computes `output_pm`; the committed light therefore changes in the tick the toggle applies, with zero internal latency. The click and the hand's switch animation pre-play immediately (Presenter); **the light changes only on committed state and the Presenter never predicts beam state** (PC-5), because the beam is the human-channel anchor and may never lie, not even for one flicker. The seat's beam id is allocated at boot by E9; the session owner enters it in the kernel binding table (`PlayerId -> {controlled entity IDs}`) through the host-only API (CR-7: "a boot step in MVP"), which is what lets `toggle_beam` carry `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`. The binding table is not saved (CR-7: sessions rebuild it), so after a restore the session owner re-enters `beam_of(player_id)` (EM-28). *Alternative considered:* the Controller allocates the beam id — rejected (CR-8). **Strobe protection is a sim guard, owned here** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; this supersedes the first-draft orchestrator ruling that routed the whole concern to the Controller's Adapter)*: the Adapter's debounce (`BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS`, owner Player Controller & Input, registry, PC-5) covers only the local human submitter, and PC-5 and Controller Open Question 18 both state that the sim-side guard "is Emitter State's to add"; with no guard here a replayed, scripted or remote submitter bypasses it and Suit SE-35's drain-sampling protection (the six-tick window) and the WCAG 2.3.1 limit rest on one client. The beam record therefore carries a canonical `last_toggle_tick` (EM-4), and `toggle_beam.validate` rejects `TOO_SOON` when `last_toggle_tick ≥ 0` and `T − last_toggle_tick < SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (12 commit ticks, owned by this GDD, derived in D.2b; it replaces the first draft's citation of the Adapter's `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` as the sim's threshold, and the Adapter constant now sits at or above it); the apply of an accepted toggle writes `last_toggle_tick = T`. *Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D32):* the same **commit-spacing rule** applies to `set_switch` for every submitter and every origin (the DOCK_STATUS glow is switched by E10, not by `set_switch`, and is exempt *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), see below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The first-draft rationale ("a sim-side `COOLDOWN` would be wall-clock-shaped") was wrong: the field is counted in ticks, is canonical, and is therefore deterministic and save-equivalent. The guard applies in both directions (a turn-OFF inside the window is also `TOO_SOON`; the rule that a turn-OFF is never rejected for charge, EM-10, is about charge, not rate); `force_off` (Suit, the DEAD tick) is not a `toggle_beam` and neither reads nor writes the field. The validate order is `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE`, `TOO_SOON`, `CHARGE_EMPTY`. An Adapter-compliant stream is never rejected **only if** `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` is at least `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`: the Adapter's registry value is 10 today, so until the Player Controller raises it to 12 (its range 10–20 allows it; 2D Lighting Ask E-E proposes the same) a human stream pressing every 10 ticks has every second press refused `TOO_SOON` (no light change, no charge drain); this is listed under I-SPACING (D.15) and AC-90b, not hidden. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
168	
169	**Commit spacing for fixtures (`set_switch`), every submitter and origin** *(user rulings: D32; default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20). 2D Lighting Ask E-E, LO-22 assigned the guard to this GDD; no exception to "the picture never disagrees with `lit`" is granted to Lighting, whose last-resort clamp may not retime a committed switch)*: `set_switch.validate` rejects with `COOLDOWN` when `last_toggle_tick ≥ 0` and the **projected commit tick** lies fewer than `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` after it. The projected commit tick is the apply tick `T_a` for an OFF that would darken a lit or armed lamp, and `arm_tick` of D.2 for an ON (a deterministic function of `T_a`, EM-12). Rules: (1) an OFF applied while the lamp is still ARMING cancels an ON that never became visible and is never refused (it is not a realised transition, EM-12, AC-80); (2) the guard measures *realised switch transitions only*: a brownout, a node failure or `served_pm` falling to 0 changes `output_pm` but is the world's doing, not the submitter's, and writes nothing; (3) the guard applies to `PLAYER` and `SYSTEM` origin alike; the MVP has **two `SYSTEM` submitters in this area and neither is a `set_switch` submitter**: Attention's breach machine submits `set_beacon` (which carries no per-emitter guard, below) and Web Map & Transit switches the DOCK_STATUS glow through the guard-free mutator E10, so a refused `COOLDOWN` is only ever seen by the `PLAYER` path at the MVP (the `SYSTEM` form of `set_switch` is kept for VS-A, where a submitter receives `COOLDOWN` like anyone and may resubmit on a later tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; (4) a same-state `SYSTEM` `set_switch` is accepted and changes nothing (below) and is not a transition; (5) `toggle_beam` keeps its domain code `TOO_SOON` (the Controller's tests and AC-90 name it), `set_switch` uses `COOLDOWN`; both are this GDD's codes under `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)`. **Consequence for the player's tap path** (stated so that no one assumes Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` 12 covers it): the tap guard spaces *submissions* by 12 ticks, while this guard spaces *commits*, and an ON commits at `arm_tick`, up to 5 ticks after its apply; so an ON tapped at tick 1201 (commit 1206) followed by an OFF tapped at 1213 (the first tap `TAP_REARM_TICKS` allows) commits at 1213, only 7 ticks after 1206, and is refused `COOLDOWN` until a tap that commits at 1218 or later (12 after 1206, subject to Interaction's own re-arm). The lamp never flickers; the refused tap changes nothing in the light, plays Interaction's failed-action cue (D.2b, delegated ruling G2) and the player taps again *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `COOLDOWN` is a domain code, not a gameplay message (no HUD text). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Lighting's flash governor is never asked to delay a committed beam or fixture flip:** at 12-tick spacing any rolling half-open 60-tick window holds at most ⌈60 / 12⌉ = 5 realised transitions, which the registry `flash_count` definition counts as ⌈5 / 2⌉ = 3 flashes (a flash is a pair of opposing transitions, counted ⌈n / 2⌉, the unit ruled 2026-10-27, X9), equal to `FLASH_MAX_PER_S` 3, so the governor's defect counter (2D Lighting LO-22, Ask E-E) stays at 0 with a transition of margin (the old 10-tick floor admitted six, three flashes with none, and seven edges, four flashes, in a window closed at both ends). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* `TOO_SOON`, `NOT_ACTIONABLE` and `NO_SUCH_EMITTER` are this GDD's own domain codes under the kernel's `VALIDATION_FAILED(domain_code)` namespace. Fixture flips are now bounded here by the commit-spacing guard above (every origin), in addition to Interaction's `TAP_REARM_TICKS` (IA-21, registry, which keeps the *submission* rate) and the Graph pulse that delays every switch-ON (EM-12); `set_beacon` carries no per-emitter guard here and Attention's breach machine, its only submitter, rate-limits itself (the residual of Open Question 25). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*

228	**EM-19 — Cone membership is fixed-point and mirror-symmetric.** A cone test uses no trigonometry, square root or float at run time (Graph LS-1(b) precedent). Directions come from a table `DIR` of Q14 unit vectors — **the table is generated at build time by a data tool outside `src/sim/emitter/` and checked in as an integer data file, never computed in the sim module** (the boot step only loads it and asserts I-MIRROR and I-OVERFLOW, so the AC-2 lint holds) — indexed by an `AIM_UNITS` angle (0 = E, counter-clockwise, screen y down, so aim 3072 = S is `(0, +16384)`), generated from one quadrant by reflection so that `DIR[2048 - a] = (-ux, uy)` **exactly**. A subject at offset `r = anchor - origin` is in the cone iff `d2 <= R²`, `D > 0` and `D² >= d2 * COS2_Q28`, with `D = rx*ux + ry*uy` (Formulas D.5); the `D > 0` guard is required (the squared test alone accepts the opposite half-plane) and `d2 = 0` is inside every cone of that emitter, the apex included. The split beam is two tests at axes `aim ± 206` units; the wedge between them never closes (I-WEDGE), so a point is in at most one cone and its contribution is never doubled. Every product has a documented bound under 2^62 and the boot assertion refuses a build that violates it (Formulas D.15). The half-angles and the 18° offset are not integral in `AIM_UNITS`, so the shape table (EM-8) carries the encoded integers; the quantisation misplaces a rim by under 0.1° (under 0.7 px at 384 px), far inside the accepted committed-versus-drawn divergence. **The symmetry property is a test, not a hope**: the exposure of a mirrored scene (x → -x, aim `a` → `2048 - a`, `flip_h` toggled) equals the mirror image of the original exactly, for the five drawn and three mirrored facings, every `CHEST_POINT` animation row and all four shapes (Acceptance Criteria).
229	
230	**EM-20 — Occlusion is integer geometry over the Layout's opaque footprints.** *(orchestrator ruling R3 — the one deliberate deviation from a routed thread's wording.)* The routed thread and the index describe occlusion as tests on "physics shapes". This GDD honours that in substance and changes the test method: the occluding shapes are the Layout's collision-footprint rectangles — walls (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH` 24 base px: face 72, cap 24, tile 48), closed door leaves, and props flagged `occludes_light` — which are the very rectangles the Layout `PROJECTOR` hands to physics and `LocomotionStep` already sweeps the avatar's box against (PC-14, PC-18). The query tests a segment against those rectangles in exact integer arithmetic (Formulas D.6) behind an **`OccluderSource` seam** (`rects_in(aabb)`, ascending rect id; `version(section_id)`, a monotone counter bumped when any opaque rectangle in the section changes); there is **no physics backend in the MVP**, and one may exist only as a test cross-check (the hybrid option). The reasons that decide it: kernel H10 (systems stay scene-tree free, headless) and CR-13 G3 (the 2D physics engine makes no determinism claim, so a physics-derived `lit` flowing into a persisted block would be a physics observation that must be recorded for replay); a direct-space-state query is valid only during the physics step, while the kernel allows this query from presentation prompts at render rate, exactly the unsafe site; and the 2D ray API is not sourceable in the pinned engine reference (its `physics.md` carries only a 3D example). *Rules.* (a) **Cells are unit squares, boxes are closed, and the rule is conservative** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft tested the closed span of cell *indices* `[x0, x1−1]`, which treats a cell as a point, so two abutting rectangles `[0,24)` and `[24,48)` left an open strip between x 23 and x 24 and an oblique ray crossed a wall seam untouched while Lighting drew a seamless shadow — a prompt lit behind a wall, a P1 lie; every worked example used an axis-aligned ray, which hid it)*: Layout's integer coordinates name pixel cells (LY-12 b), and a cell is a unit square centred on its integer coordinate. The box D.6 tests for an occupied span `(sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1)` returned by `rects_in` (= the stored `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` as `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`) is the closed continuous box `[sx0 − ½, sx1 + ½] × [sy0 − ½, sy1 + ½]`, computed in **doubled coordinates** (every segment endpoint × 2) as the integer box `[2·sx0 − 1, 2·sx1 + 1] × [2·sy0 − 1, 2·sy1 + 1]` — in the stored rectangle's own terms `[2·x0 − 1, 2·x1 − 1] × [2·y0 − 1, 2·y1 − 1]`. Abutting rectangles share a box face (`[0,24)` and `[24,48)` give doubled x `[−1, 47]` and `[47, 95]`, touching at 47), so no wall seam, door-leaf/jamb joint or corner join leaves a strip; a segment that touches a box (a corner graze, an edge-on pass) is blocked; light does not leak around a corner. A segment endpoint is an integer cell, doubled to an even number against odd box bounds, so it is never exactly on a box face and is inside a box if and only if its cell is occupied. This convention is stated once, here and in D.6; Layout's occupied-span algebra (registry `rect_algebra_closed_span`, LY-12 b, D.2) remains the definition of *which cells are occupied* and of the anchor lint and is unchanged (routed to Layout: its rule text "the conservative closed test is applied to the occupied span" must read "the cell-unit box of the occupied span", Cross-References). (b) **Anchors must be at least `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` (1 base px) outside every occluding rectangle** (Chebyshev distance in cells from the occupied span, Layout D.2: a wall stored [408,432), whose occupied span is x 408..431, admits anchors at x = 407 and x = 432 and rejects 408 through 431; registry: `rect_algebra_closed_span`, the Layout's half-open convention), checked by authoring lint at registration. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **What the clearance means under the unit-square convention:** at 1 the anchor's centre is half a pixel (one doubled unit) outside the occluding box face, with its own cell directly adjacent to the wall, which guarantees that the segment's start is outside every box; a clearance of 0 would put the anchor inside the box. The check covers **every emitter anchor, not only subject anchors**: fixture, lantern and beacon placements at instantiate (a data-load lint) and FAULT_GLOW anchors at creation (EM-17); an emitter anchored on its own wall footprint would light nothing in its room and, in the first draft, raised no diagnostic. An anchor found strictly inside a footprint at run time is treated as blocked from every emitter (fails safe to dark) and increments `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`. (c) **Actors and horrors never occlude.** A shadow with no occluder is a stage-2 sanity symptom (art bible 3.2 open item: it should not cast an occluding shadow) and must stay an unambiguous tell; so a horror standing in a beam leaves the beam unchanged and the subject beyond it lit. (d) **Door state is read from the Layout projection of the Graph's `door_state`** (Graph LS-6: the Graph owns door state and opening `area`) — the same door-leaf rectangle `collide` uses (PC-3, PC-18 test 7: same-tick door response) — so there is one source for collision and light, derived from the Graph in the same tick, and Emitter State holds **no door flag**. The door-leaf rectangle is the Layout's `door_leaf_gap` projection (Layout D.5, LY-9): `leaf_w` is continuous in the Graph's opening area and `leaf_w` 0 yields no rectangle, so no open-fraction threshold exists; `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is deprecated and unused. (e) A door interactable registers **two** face subjects, one per face, each `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside the leaf, so a closed leaf blocks the other side's emitters from each face subject (Interaction's registration; EM-21). (f) No glass or translucent occluders in the MVP. (g) The occlusion segment starts at the occlusion origin of EM-6 (the foot, for the beam). The wording this implies for the index and the kernel is routed in Cross-References. *Alternatives considered:* a physics-space query against a dedicated occluder layer — rejected (above); reusing a rendering occluder object as the sim's occluder — rejected outright, it is Lighting's rendering object and the sim never reads it.

232	**EM-21 — Subjects register; each has one anchor; an unregistered ref answers like an unlit one.** Anything that asks "am I lit" registers a **subject** with `register_subject(ref, kind, anchor_px, section_id)` (E6) and withdraws it with `unregister_subject(ref)` (E7). Subject kinds: OBJECT (an interaction anchor), ACTOR (the foot origin, *read* from `body.state` each tick, not supplied; its `section_id` and `body_id` are read the same way from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)`, BDY-29, so the owner's exposure is attributed to the section the foot stands in and moves with it across a door), HORROR, ITEM (loose items). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The subject's single `anchor_px` is the only sampled point: a large object half in a beam is lit iff its anchor is (the same one-point model as `REACH_PX` and focus scoring, PC-6, and the cheapest symmetric one). Sections are never point-sampled; they aggregate by emitter list (`section_emission`, EM-27). `moving` is a per-registration flag: ACTOR and HORROR subjects are always moving; an ITEM registers static (a carried item is unregistered at pickup and re-registered at drop); only moving registrations count against `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`. **The owner stands in their own light** *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's SD-7 adopted with the checkpoint fix CP-9 — as first proposed it excluded the owner's beam from the owner's lux, so a player alone with the lamp on would have read `lux` 0 to Horror, the opposite of P3)*: the owner's own beam contributes its **full `output_pm`** — the d = 0 apex value, which EM-19 already places inside every cone — to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm`, independent of facing and of occlusion, so the owner's self-lux never flips with the way they face; it is not added to the owner's `act_lux_pm` (the player is never the target of their own verb). Attention reads the beam as *emission* (`emitters()`, `section_emission`) and does not add the same beam again to the owner's lux (EM-27). Every other beam lights the owner, and the owner's beam lights everyone else, by the ordinary cone test. **An unregistered ref answers exactly like an unlit registered one** *(orchestrator ruling: SD-16 adopted — a P4 requirement)*: `lux(ref)` is 0 and `lit(ref)` is false in release builds, so the Perception Filter's phantom targets (kernel Open Question 14) cost Interaction the same check as real unlit ones and the query cannot become an existence oracle that undermines the phantom-loot hallucination. A debug-only `registered(ref)` exists for tests and the Debug Overlay. Registration over `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` returns false, increments `emitter_subjects_overflow` and the subject reads dark (fails safe); a duplicate registration is a no-op returning false. **Runtime overflow is a content or budget defect, never a gameplay state** *(creative-director CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 3)*: failing safe to dark is the right behaviour for a subject the table cannot hold, but a real object sitting visibly inside a beam that refuses to prompt breaks design test 1 (the honest edge) and the P4 "reach for it" falsifier, because the player reads a real lit object as a hallucination. So the caps are held upstream by budgets, not discovered at run time (EM-24, D.15 I-CAPS (d)), and the two counters `emitter_subjects_overflow` and `emitter_moving_overflow` ship in release builds as telemetry (the probe counter went with the probes, EM-24) (a counter in the diagnostics block, not only a debug assertion), so a budget breach in a playtest or live build is visible and reportable. The subject table fields are below. Registrations are canonical (EM-28, R16): registrants (Interaction, Horror, Suit) own the thing registered and re-register idempotently in their own `post_restore`, which `restore_after` `emitter.state` allows.

The frame each registrant passes is to be confirmed by Interaction and Horror (Open Question 29) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

247	**EM-22 — `lit(subject)`: threshold, hysteresis and the beacon exception.** `lit(ref)` is a hysteresis filter over `act_lux_pm` (Formulas D.8): it becomes true when `act_lux_pm >= LIT_ON_PM`, becomes false when `act_lux_pm < LIT_OFF_PM`, and holds between. Placeholders `LIT_ON_PM` 150 (range 100–300) and `LIT_OFF_PM` 120 (60–140), the `LIT_THRESHOLD_PM` family **owned by the technical-artist** (art bible 7.0: "the illumination threshold that enables prompt and inspect-card drawing"), confirmed against the rendered edge in the Lighting spike (8.12 step 2). A newly registered subject starts unlit and is evaluated at the next `emitter.place`. A hard-edged rim is a *step* (a full-output rim contributes `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` then 0 across one pixel), which the 150/120 hysteresis never sees; rim chatter while a beam sweeps is held by the Controller's committed-aim quantisation (`AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` 32 units) and `FOCUS_STICKY_MARGIN` (PC-6), and the hysteresis bites only for dimmed or soft light (brownout, waning glowsticks, fixture pools). There is **no dwell** (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` fixed at 0): keeping `lit` true after the light went would be a window where the sim says lit and the world is dark, a P1 lie. `lit(ref)` and `lux(ref)` are separate answers because the beacon's sweep must not strobe prompts (EM-16). **The hysteresis bit is canonical** (checkpoint ruling CP-2): `lit(ref)` depends on last tick's answer, and a subject whose `act_lux_pm` sits between `LIT_OFF_PM` and `LIT_ON_PM` has no other source for its bit, so by EM-4's own definition the bit is a discrete fact — one bit per registered subject, at most `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` bits, snapshotted and hashed. `post_restore` rebuilds `lux_pm`, `act_lux_pm` and `top_emitter_id` from the restored emitters and **keeps the bit**; the next `emitter.place` applies hysteresis normally. A subject saved at 130 permille and lit is therefore lit after the restore, and Interaction's `validate` at T+1 reads the same answer in the live run and the restored run (kernel G4). *(orchestrator ruling: the systems-designer's canonical bitset is the rule. Rejected alternative: rebuild every bit against `LIT_ON_PM` in `post_restore` (the earlier ruling R6) — a subject between the thresholds would flip from lit to unlit across a restore, `validate` at T+1 would accept in one run and reject `NOT_LIT` in the other, and canonical state downstream would diverge.)* Interaction's `validate` and the HUD prompt call this same `lit(ref)`, so the prompt never lies by omission (PC-6).
248	
249	**EM-23 — The order of work inside `emitter.place`; static and dynamic layers; no subscriptions.** The hook does, in this order and nothing else: **W0** read upstream (`controller.state` and `body.state` for bound seats; the Layout `OccluderSource.version(section_id)`; the Graph's `served_pm` and `node(id)`; on Graph ticks the Graph's `failures(filter)`), and rewrite the derived `section_id` and `body_id` of each BEAM record and ACTOR subject from Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` and `body_of_actor(actor_id)` (a tick in which the foot crosses a door moves the beam's section in that tick) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **W1** lifecycle (DEAD force-off, deployable aging, evict-wane (D.9b) and removal, `arm_tick` arming, fault-glow reconciliation); **W2** derive every emitter in ascending id (origin, aim, reach, `output_pm`, record `lit`); **W3** find the static-layer rows whose inputs changed; **W4** update them by deltas, in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), **synchronously — nothing is left pending past W4** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; **W5** the dynamic layer for every subject (with the owner-beam special case of EM-21: the owner's own beam adds its apex value to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` with no cone or occlusion test); **W6** saturating sums, hysteresis, write the subject table, record the tick's counted work; **W7** write dirty keys (EM-26). The **static layer** (FIXTURE, NODE_LANTERN, FAULT_GLOW, resting DEPLOYABLE) is cached as **per-pair contribution rows** `(emitter id, subject ref) → {d, f_pm, c}` (a row exists only while the emitter is in radius and unblocked) plus, per subject, an **unsaturated** raw sum `Σ c`, clamped to 1000 only when the answer is read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The first draft cached a saturated partial sum, which is exact for *adding* an emitter (`min(1000, min(1000, a) + b) = min(1000, a + b)`) but cannot *remove* one (a saturated 1000 has forgotten what it summed), so every output change would have forced a full re-evaluation of the subject; with the pair rows every change is a delta: (i) an emitter's **output** changes (to or from 0, a brownout step, inrush): `c = ⌊output_pm × f_pm / 1000⌋` is recomputed from the stored `f_pm` with no geometry, and an `output_pm` of 0 stores `c` = 0 with no multiply while the rows (the geometry) are kept, so a blackout is a zeroing of rows and not a re-evaluation of the ship, and switching back on is a delta too; (ii) an emitter's integer **reach** changes (a waning stick): `d` and `f_pm` are recomputed for its rows and rows beyond the new reach are dropped, with no occlusion test (reach only shrinks, so no pair is added); (iii) an emitter is **created** (its candidate subjects are tested radius first, then occlusion, and rows are added) or **removed** (its rows are dropped); (iv) a subject is **registered or moved** (it is tested against the static emitters in range); (v) an **occluder** changes (only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region are re-tested, below); (vi) the layer is **cold** (`post_restore`, section instantiate: everything is built). Rows are derived, never hashed, rebuilt in ascending (emitter id, subject ref), and sized by ADR candidate 4; a row-table overflow changes cost, never an answer, and increments `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`; the **dynamic layer** (BEAM, BEACON, which rotate or translate every tick) is recomputed per tick with the cheapest rejects first — radius, then cone, then the occlusion test. A subject's static rows are updated when `emitter.place` *observes* a change in what it read last tick: the section's `OccluderSource.version(...)` changed, an emitter's `output_pm` or integer `reach_px` changed, an emitter was created or removed, or the subject moved. **Never by subscription**: kernel CR-10 ("simulation systems never subscribe; sim-to-sim is ordered step reads or commands"); dirty keys are the notification channel for PRESENTATION and friends, not an input to this block. A pose-unchanged skip (a dynamic emitter whose origin, aim, output, shape and occlusion origin equal last tick's skips re-evaluation) is a pure optimisation and changes no answer. A static emitter's cost is paid when something changes, not every tick; a glowstick's reach steps by one px every 50 ticks while it wanes (3600 ticks over 72 px, D.9), so the rows of the subjects in its range are recomputed that often (D.14, S5). **Narrowing rule for door leaves** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `OccluderSource.version(section_id)` says only *that* something in the section changed, and a leaf bump arrives at the Graph's step rate while a door travels (roughly ten per second), so a response that re-tests every pair of the section would cost 11,522 units per bump (D.14, S1: 14 × `T_sub` 823) against `B` 10,000 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The Emitter therefore re-tests only pairs whose segment bounding box meets the changed region: **(L)** Layout publishes the changed region with the bump (ask E-N, a union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; a structural bump — build, attach, detach, discard, restore — reports `ALL`), or, if Layout declines, **(D)** every pair whose segment bounding box meets a door-leaf pre-filter box of its section is tagged *dynamic* and evaluated every tick in the dynamic layer, which costs the same amount every tick instead of once per bump (priced in S1). ADR candidate 4 chooses between L and D on Layout's answer; both fit the budget. A restore-time bump (Layout's `post_restore`, version 1 to 2) is treated as a leaf-region change over that section's leaf boxes, not as `ALL`, because structural geometry is valid straight after `restore()` (Layout LY-26 b). **The contract is "never stale", and the rebuild is synchronous** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; resolves the question that D.13's age bound left open)*: W3 and W4 finish every update inside the tick, before W6 writes the table, so there is no pending state and the D.13 bound (age 0 or 1 tick) holds for every reader, including Interaction's `validate` at T−1 and its six-tick re-check, Attention and Horror. A tick whose updates exceed the ceiling of D.14 still completes them, increments `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling` and is a hitch to be removed by content or by the ordered fallbacks, never deferred. **Alternative (b), rejected and recorded for ADR candidate 4:** a deterministic counted-unit cap per tick, a widened staleness bound and a fail-safe lit-or-dark rule for pending subjects. It was rejected because (1) `lit` would then depend on a rebuild queue that is derived, not canonical, so a snapshot restored mid-queue (which rebuilds cold and complete) would answer differently from the uninterrupted run — kernel G4 broken in exactly the way the old probe budget broke it (EM-24); (2) a fail-safe-dark rule would blink the prompts of a whole room on every door bump; and (3) it would rewrite the age bound that three designed GDDs already build on. The ceiling's named owner is the technical-director; the exposure spike reports it (AC-53).
250	
251	**EM-24 — Counted work, not wall-clock; the caps.** The per-tick exposure cost is bounded by **counted work units**, never by timing — a time-based governor would be nondeterministic. The caps (all *placeholder, owner technical-director, confirmed by the exposure spike and the Interaction / Derelict Authoring content counts*; never inherited from a default of 64): `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS` 192 (derived from the MVP slice's 14 compartments — home-ship 5, derelict A 4, derelict B 5 — their verb-bearing nodes, doors counted twice for their two face subjects, loose items, actors and horror subjects; Formulas D.14; *orchestrator pick: the systems-designer's 192 over the technical-director's 128, because doors register two subjects (EM-20 e) and the MVP Graph's node count supports a larger interactable set*), `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` 16 (the 17th moving registration returns false, increments `emitter_moving_overflow` and the subject reads dark, the same fail-safe as `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`), `MAX_EMITTERS` 96, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8, `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` 4, `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` 10. **The caps are content budgets, held at data load, not gameplay states** *(CD-GDD-ALIGN concerns 1 and 3)*: the MVP slice has exactly 8 live faults world-wide, of which a welded body carries at most 6 simultaneous glow rows (registry `mvp_fault_allocation`); I-CAPS therefore requires `MAX_FAULT_GLOW` to be at least the most simultaneous glowing authored faults on one body plus 25 % (⌈1.25 × 6⌉ = 8; the cap of 10 keeps 2 of headroom), and requires the **dynamic registrants** that arrive after boot to be held to per-category budgets owned by their authors: Derelict Authoring owns the budget for authored OBJECT and ITEM subjects and for dropped loot and spawned salvage per section, Horror Entities owns the horror-subject budget (`HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` 2 (Horror Entities, registry), all moving; Horror's `horror_subject_count` holds `HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` + `A_max` 4 = 6 ≤ `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`) and the share of `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS` it may use, Interaction owns the dropped-item registrations, and the deployable budget is `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` + `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING` (D.14, D.15 I-CAPS (d)). A runtime overflow of any cap is a defect of one of those budgets, is counted by a release-build telemetry counter (`emitter_subjects_overflow`, `emitter_moving_overflow`, `emitter_fault_glow_overcap`, `emitter_fault_glow_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evictions`, `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow`, and, added by the 2026-10-27 design review, `emitter_create_refused`, `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor`, `emitter_anchor_clearance_fail`, `emitter_reach_invalid`, `emitter_actor_section_none`, `emitter_pair_rows_overflow`, `emitter_rebuild_over_ceiling`, and, added by the re-review, `emitter_dock_status_missing`, `emitter_invalid_transition` and the playtest counters of the metric stub) as well as asserted in debug, and is never something a design relies on. `EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS` is **0.4 ms P99** for `emitter.place` plus all exposure evaluation (placeholder, spike on the Release export template; the kernel's `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold and P3's target is ≤ 2.0 ms P99 with the Graph at 0.5 ms and Controller + Body about 0.3 ms). It is the *steady-state* budget; the named rare-event scenarios of D.14 are held to `EXPOSURE_TICK_CEILING_MS` (hot class) and `COLD_REBUILD_CEILING_MS` (cold class), both owned by the technical-director. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Mandatory work (the dynamic layer, static rebuilds, the subject table) is never skipped. **Creation at `MAX_EMITTERS`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the first draft had no run-time rule at the global cap)*: when the record count equals `MAX_EMITTERS` a creation is **refused**, never made by removing a light that has a physical cause. E1 refuses the section's remaining records, `spawn_deployable` returns false (the item was already spent, Item DB rule (c)), and a FAULT_GLOW reconciliation creates nothing for the lowest-ranked descriptors; each refusal increments `emitter_create_refused` (release telemetry, per kind) and asserts in debug. Within one pass creations are admitted in `priority` order, highest first (BEAM 255, BEACON 200, FIXTURE 120, DEPLOYABLE 100, FAULT_GLOW 80, NODE_LANTERN 60; ties by ascending creation order), so the light the player most needs is the one kept; the seat beams are never refused, because their slots are reserved (I-CAPS (a) counts the bound seats). The cap is a content budget held by I-CAPS (a); the rule exists so that a breach is deterministic, counted and visible, never a gameplay state. **Probes and `lit_by(point)` are deferred to Vertical Slice A** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: no MVP consumer calls them (Horror HE-19 and HE-25 use Layout `room_at` / `room_adjacency` and make no `probe()` call, Attention AT-4 makes none, Sanity no longer uses `lit_static` (deferred to VS-A, EM-25), and Interaction's re-checks are `lit(ref)` lookups), so `probe`, `lit_by`, `MAX_PROBES_PER_TICK`, `W_PROBE`, `probes_allowed` and the probe counter are removed from the MVP read view, budget and acceptance criteria. 410	### D.1b Dock status glow sizing *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: X2)*
411	
412	The `dock_status_glow` sizing is defined as the set of constraints the self-powered DOCK_STATUS fixture (EM-11) must satisfy, with D.1 and D.7 as the formulas:
413	
414	`output_pm = DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM` while `switch_on` (self-powered: `armed` 1, `live` 1, `served_pm` 1000, so D.1 reduces to `base_pm`); the console subject at distance `d_c ≤ DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX` from the glow origin is lit iff `c(d_c) = ⌊ DOCK_STATUS_BASE_PM × F(d_c, R) / 1000 ⌋ ≥ LIT_ON_PM`, `R = DOCK_STATUS_REACH_PX`, `F(d, R) = ⌊1000 × (R − d) / R⌋`

416	**Constraints.** (C1) `R ≥ REACH_MIN_PX` 24 (I-REACH). (C2) the console is lit with margin at the farthest allowed placement: `c(DOCK_STATUS_CONSOLE_MAX_PX) ≥ LIT_ON_PM` plus a margin that absorbs a placement tolerance. 545	### D.7 Illumination
546	
547	The `illumination` formula is defined as:
548	
549	`c = ⌊ output_pm × f / 1000 ⌋`, SOFT: `f = F(d, R)`; HARD: `f = EDGE_FLOOR_PM + ⌊(1000 − EDGE_FLOOR_PM) × F(d, R) / 1000⌋`; `F(d, R) = ⌊1000 × (R − d) / R⌋` (curve id LINEAR, the MVP default); `d = max{k : SQ[k] ≤ d2}`; `lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c)`; `act_lux_pm = min(1000, Σ c over gates_actions emitters)`; actionable radius `r_lit = max{ d ∈ 0..R : c(d) ≥ LIT_ON_PM }` over the same integer chain (−1 when `c(0) < LIT_ON_PM`), found by binary search because `c` is monotone non-increasing in `d`, and **published from the sim per emitter as `r_lit_px`** (derived on an output or reach change; the closed form ⌊R × (output_pm − LIT_ON_PM) / output_pm⌋ is retired) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
550	
551	**Variables:**
552	
553	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
554	|---|---|---|---|---|
555	| `output_pm` | int | 0..1000 | D.1, D.3, D.9 (constant), D.11, `BEAM_BASE_PM` | the emitter's steady output |
556	| `d` | int px | 0..R | `SQ` table: 385 squares, binary search, 9 probes | exact integer floor of the distance from the origin (the chest for the beam); no square root, no float |
557	| `R` | int px | 24..384 | `reach_px` | current reach (D.9 for a waning stick) |
558	| `F` | int | 0..1000 | curve id (data) | 1000 at the apex, 0 at `R`; a replacement curve (a 17-knot table, linear interpolation on `u = ⌊d × 1024 / R⌋`) keeps the signature and must stay monotone, integer, with non-negative operands (R15) |
559	| `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` | int | 250 (160..400) | placeholder, owner technical-artist, confirmed by the Lighting spike | the HARD-class contribution kept at the rim; jointly bound with `LIT_ON_PM` by I-EDGE |
560	| `LIT_ON_PM` | int | 150 (100..300) | D.8 | the turn-on threshold |
561	| `r_lit_px` | int px | −1..R | calculated, published per emitter | the largest `d` whose integer chain gives `c ≥ LIT_ON_PM`; what Lighting draws a soft pool's readable boundary at, and what a prompt agrees with *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
562	
563	**Output Range:** `c` 0..1000, `lux_pm` and `act_lux_pm` 0..1000 (saturating; addition commutes, so there is no order dependence). There is no ambient term (`AMBIENT_PM` 0). The owner's own beam adds its full `output_pm` (the d = 0 apex value) to the owner's ACTOR `lux_pm` and nothing to its `act_lux_pm` (EM-21). **Example:** wide beam `output_pm` 1000, `d2` 43,264 → `d` 208 (208² ≤ 43,264 < 209²), `R` 288: `F` ⌊1000 × 80 / 288⌋ = 277, `f` 250 + ⌊750 × 277 / 1000⌋ = 457, `c` 457; at the rim `c` = `EDGE_FLOOR_PM` 250 (lit), and a beam at `output_pm` 600 has rim `c` 150 (lit) while 599 gives 149 (unlit), the ⌈`LIT_ON_PM` × 1000 / `EDGE_FLOOR_PM`⌉ = 600 consequence. SOFT fixture `R` 144, `output_pm` 1000: `d` 122 → `F` 152 (lit), `d` 123 → 145 (unlit), `r_lit` 122 (the chain: `d` 122 lit, `d` 123 unlit; at output 1000 the closed form ⌊144 × 850 / 1000⌋ = 122 agrees with the chain for every `R` from 24 to 384, but at output 450 the closed form gives 96 where the chain gives 95; over `R` = 24..384 step 24 and `output_pm` 151..1000 the closed form ran 1 px high in 1,405 of 13,600 cases and never low, the review's coarser sweep found 219 of 5,100, so Lighting's drawn pool edge would have sat 1 px outside the actionable edge and used the whole AC-56 tolerance) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Sum: beam 457 + a lamp of `output_pm` 848 at `d` 100 (`F` 305, `c` ⌊848 × 305 / 1000⌋ = 258) → `lux_pm` 715; adding a fixture at `d` 60 (`c` 583) gives 1298 → 1000. Alone with the lamp on, the owner reads `lux_pm` 1000.
564	
565	### D.8 Lit with hysteresis
566	
567	The `lit_hysteresis` formula is defined as:
568	
569	`lit′ = (act_lux_pm ≥ LIT_ON_PM) ∨ (lit ∧ act_lux_pm ≥ LIT_OFF_PM)`; a stateless `lit_on = act_lux_pm ≥ LIT_ON_PM` form is reserved for the VS-A `probe(body_id, point)` (EM-24) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
570	
571	**Variables:**
572	
573	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
574	|---|---|---|---|---|
575	| `act_lux_pm` | int | 0..1000 | D.7 | action-gating light (the BEACON does not gate) |
576	| `lit` | bool | 0/1 | canonical, one bit per subject (EM-22) | last tick's answer; kept across a restore |
577	| `LIT_ON_PM` | int | 150 (100..300) | placeholder, owner technical-artist (art bible 7.0), confirmed by the Lighting spike | turn-on |
578	| `LIT_OFF_PM` | int | 120 (60..140), `< LIT_ON_PM` | same | turn-off; there is no dwell (`LIT_OFF_DWELL_TICKS` fixed at 0) |
579	
580	**Output Range:** bool. The band in px at a soft rim is ⌊`R` × (`LIT_ON_PM` − `LIT_OFF_PM`) / `output_pm`⌋: 4 px for a fixture (R 144), 2 px for a glowstick (R 96); a hard rim is a step (457 → 0 across one pixel), so hysteresis only matters for dimmed or soft light. **Example:** 160 → lit; 130 → still lit; 119 → unlit; 140 → still unlit; 151 → lit. A subject saved lit at 130 is lit after the restore (the bit is canonical). A lamp browning from `served_pm` 950 to 780 moves a subject at `d` 122 from `c` 144 (still lit) to 118 (unlit).

an output of 0 sets `r_lit_px` −1 with no search; `N_rl` ≤ `N_dirty`); `B = EXPOSURE_BUDGET_MS × 10⁶ / U_OP_NS`, `C_hot = EXPOSURE_TICK_CEILING_MS × 10⁶ / U_OP_NS`, `C_cold = COLD_REBUILD_CEILING_MS × 10⁶ / U_OP_NS`; static-layer terms `T_out = ρ × W_DELTA + N_keys × W_PUB`, `T_reach = ρ × W_CON + N_keys × W_PUB`, `T_leaf = P_leaf × (W_REJ + K_OCC × W_SEG + W_RECTS)`, `T_new = N_cs × W_REJ + ρ × (W_CON + K_OCC × W_SEG + W_RECTS)` (VS-A creation only: the MVP builds nothing after `init_world`); 806	
807	- **If a segment only touches a rectangle (corner graze), crosses a seam between abutting rectangles (wall run, door-leaf/jamb joint) or passes through a corner shared by two diagonal rectangles**: it is blocked, because cells are unit squares and abutting boxes share a face (EM-20 a, D.6); an oblique ray never slips through a seam. An anchor within `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` of a footprint fails the registration lint, and an anchor found strictly inside a footprint at run time is blocked from every emitter and reads dark. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
808	- **If a door closes mid-channel**: the next `emitter.place` observes the `OccluderSource.version(section_id)` change, rebuilds the static layer for the section, the target reads dark and the owner's re-check aborts the channel within 6 ticks.
809	- **If a door is partly open**: the door-leaf rectangle is the Layout's `door_leaf_gap` projection (`leaf_w` continuous in the Graph's opening area; `leaf_w` 0 yields no rectangle), so light passes exactly the gap the leaf leaves; `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is deprecated and unused.
810	- **If a horror or an actor stands between an emitter and a subject**: nothing is occluded and the subject beyond stays lit; a shadow with no occluder is a stage-2 symptom and must stay an unambiguous tell.
811	- **If a carried item is dropped**: it re-registers as a static ITEM subject at the drop anchor and is evaluated at the next `emitter.place` (it was unregistered at pickup, EM-21).
812	- **If the subject is an unregistered ref (including a Perception Filter phantom target)**: `lux` 0 and `lit` false, indistinguishable from a registered unlit subject in release, so the query is no existence oracle; `registered(ref)` exists in debug builds only.
813	- **If registrations exceed `MAX_EXPOSURE_SUBJECTS`, or moving registrations exceed `MAX_MOVING_SUBJECTS`**: `register_subject` returns false, `emitter_subjects_overflow` (or `emitter_moving_overflow`) increments in release builds as telemetry, the subject reads dark (fails safe) and a debug assertion fires. **This is a content or budget bug and never a gameplay state**: a real object inside a beam that refuses to prompt would break the honest edge (design test 1) and read as a hallucination (the P4 "reach for it" falsifier), so the per-category budgets (Derelict Authoring: authored objects, items, dropped loot and spawned salvage; Horror Entities: horror subjects; Interaction: dropped items) are held by I-CAPS (d), a breach seen in telemetry is fixed in the owning budget, and no design may rely on the refusal. **If a source calls `probe()` or `lit_by()` in the MVP**: the lint fails the build (EM-24; both are deferred to VS-A). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
814	- **If a subject's `body_id` differs from an emitter's (a detached section)**: that emitter contributes 0 (EM-30); cross-body light is a Ship Body question for VS-A.
815	- **If in-view emitters exceed Lighting's budget (24 non-shadow + 6 shadow, 8 lanterns)**: the sim never culls by view, a cut light still exposes (P3), a debug assertion reports it and `priority` makes Lighting's cut reproducible; the authoring lint should have refused the content.
816	
817	**Deployables, beacon and fault glow**
818	
819	- **If a glowstick lands on a dormant or unknown section**: `spawn_deployable` is a no-op returning false, Interaction has already spent the item and no light ever existed. **If it lands inside a closed room**: it lights that room only (the walls occlude).
820	- **If two glowsticks overlap**: contributions saturate at 1000 and each wanes on its own clock. **If a spawn exceeds `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE`**: the new stick spawns in full (Class B never rejects) and the lowest-id non-evicting deployable of the same kind enters a visible evict-wane (D.9b): its reach falls from where it is to 24 px over `GLOWSTICK_EVICT_WANE_S` (10 s) and only then is it removed, so no light dies with no physical cause; `emitter_deployable_evictions` increments. **If an eviction would exceed `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_EVICTING`**: the oldest evicting stick completes at once, `emitter_deployable_evict_overflow` increments and a debug assertion fires (a budget defect, I-SUPPLY). **If a section is discarded with live deployables**: they are removed with it.
821	- **If `life_remaining_ticks` reaches 0**: the record is removed that tick and its id retired, the subjects it lit re-read next tick, and there is no fade (the waning already took the reach to 24 px).
822	- **If `set_beacon` turns the beacon on**: it starts from the angle the pure function gives at that tick, not phase 0; off, it contributes 0 from the next tick. **If its bus is dead**: `output_pm` is 0 (D.1) while the aim stays a pure function of `T`.
823	- **If the beacon sweeps a subject in an otherwise dark room**: `lux_pm` is above 0 for 14 or 15 of every 128 ticks (by phase; the same count in two runs and across a restore) and `lit` stays false, so no prompt strobes and no channel aborts at the sweep rate.

826	- **If a `mod_lamp` sits on the lowest `power_tier`** (Derelict Authoring OQ-V4): its output is `base_pm × served_pm / 1000` (D.1); the lowest tier is the first shed under a shortfall, so it reads dimmer only while its tier is under-served (`served_pm` < 1000) and identical to any other lamp at full supply; whether a given `served_pm` reads *visibly* dimmer is the Lighting spike's to confirm.

878	**Circularity check.** The index's circular-dependency note says "Lighting exposes an emitter registry; Attention reads it and publishes an attention level; the filament renderer reads both. Lighting never reads Attention." This GDD resolves the first clause: the registry is **`emitter.state`'s read view**, which Lighting and Attention both read, and Lighting never writes it (a wording refresh owed to the index, Cross-References). No cycle exists: Emitter State reads the Graph, the Controller, Body and Layout and none of them reads it back (the Controller's PC-6 *calls* the exposure query, a read, from `validate`, and the Graph reads nothing from here); Attention's `set_beacon` is a `SYSTEM` command applied at T+1.
879	
880	**Engine reference gaps (Godot 4.7.2, pinned).** `docs/engine-reference/godot/` has **no `scripting.md` or `core.md`** (its `modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui): GDScript integer-math cost, `RefCounted` state blocks and packed-array performance are **NOT SOURCEABLE** from the reference and every cost number here is a model parameter for the spike. The 2D physics ray API is likewise **NOT SOURCEABLE** (`modules/physics.md` carries only a 3D example); EM-20 removes the dependency. 2D physics is unchanged since 4.3 (the reference says so for 4.6). Sourced breaking changes that bite this module (`breaking-changes.md`): 4.7 typed-return overrides need an explicit `return` on every path (a typed-return virtual in an emitter-kind base class would break — avoid virtual dispatch on the hot path); a write to one element of a packed array does not call the property setter, so dirty keys are marked explicitly in the mutators, never in setters (kernel CR-8, Graph LS-18); `duplicate()` is not deep, so snapshot copies use plain-data copies or `duplicate_deep()`. Light2D behaviour in 4.5–4.7 is Lighting's HIGH-risk gap, not this system's (it never reads one). No ADR exists yet; candidates are listed in the Overview.

A beam is a wedge with a **hard outer edge exactly at its reach** (3 screen px of edge, then a soft interior falloff) in the Tungsten hue every human light uses (art bible 4.2); the four shapes, the fan, the deployable pool, the glowstick, the fixture and the beacon are the art bible 8.3 rows (lines 1079–1086) carried verbatim into the shape table, with two rows this GDD adds (lantern, fault glow) and the HARD / SOFT curve classes owed back to 8.3 (Cross-References). A glowstick is Chemlight `#86B896`, steady and then visibly smaller (art bible 3.2: "steady, then waning"); a fixture never flickers (the cryo-bay lamp's gutter is Lighting's, art bible 8.11 flag 2); the dock status glow is a small, dim, steady fixture whose luminance and hue the art-director keeps apart from the visible-unknown lamp (a Lighting `hue_class` token and the luminance separation are owed by the art-director and art bible 7.0 note; X2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; a node lantern is the glow of a running machine in that loop's own hue at its machinery node (art bible 8.3 emission rule, 8.10 flag 8); fault glows are point sources (ember, power arc, cyan O₂ mist) taken from the Failure & Trail descriptor-to-glow table. Everything is drawn from `emitter.state` and nothing else.
943	
944	**What Lighting reads, and must not do.** Lighting reads the per-emitter read view (`id, kind, subkind, shape_id, origin_px, aim_units, half_angle_units, reach_px, r_lit_px, curve_class, output_pm, hue_class, lit, section_id, body_id, priority`, AC-46b) and `shapes()`, and it conforms to them: a texture's reach equals `reach_px` ± 1 px for every hard-edged row; a soft pool's readable boundary is drawn at the published actionable radius `r_lit_px` (D.7, an exact sim value) ± 1 px, so that a prompt appears exactly where the pool visibly ends (the sim/render agreement, AC-55 and AC-56, the load-bearing P1 test of the lighting stack); a dimmed emitter is drawn dimmer in proportion to `output_pm` (a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served, Graph D.6). Lighting **owns** the light textures, ambient and `CanvasModulate`, shadow-slot assignment (lint hypotheses: at most 6 shadow-casting, 24 non-shadow and 8 node lanterns in view, art bible 8.10 and 8.11 flags 2 and 8; "emitters are cut before occlusion"), flicker and gutter, the per-light flash clamp (`flash_count` ≤ 3 per rolling 1 s, pipeline PR-13), and the decoy visuals of the Perception Filter. Lighting **must not**: write an emitter or any block; tell the sim a light is "culled"; give a decoy, a false lamp state or a flicker any query effect (the query reads `output_pm`, not the picture; AC-5a); move the true edge of a real light (art bible Principle 1; the stage-2 "cone seems to reach further" symptom is a **decoy glow past the true edge** with a palette leak, never a wider revealing radius, Cross-References refresh to 4.4); or draw a shadow with no occluder from a horror (actors and horrors never occlude, art bible 3.2, EM-20 c). Occlusion shadows follow the same footprint rectangles the query uses (one source for collision, light and shadow), and the same cell convention: Lighting's occluder polygon for a stored rectangle `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` is the continuous rectangle covering exactly those pixel cells, and an integer position is the centre of its cell (EM-20 a), so a drawn shadow has no seam where the query has none *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the shadow origin versus the sim's foot segment (EM-6, CP-5) is Open Question 5.
945	
946	**What Audio hears.** Audio keys off the `E/<emitter id>` dirty keys (EM-26) and the Presenter's own pre-play, and reads **no exposure** (it does not call `lux` or `lit`). The beam switch click and the wall-switch click pre-play on input (PC-5; the light itself lands on commit); a lamp hum rises across the 0–5 tick switch latency so the warm-up reads as a ship lamp, not lag; a bank switched together draws inrush and the neighbouring dip is a legitimate, audible, player-caused flicker (Graph `INRUSH_PM`); a glowstick may thin a faint chemical hiss as it wanes and ends with a soft quiet; the beacon's sweep has a rotation cadence at `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` 128 (2.13 s); fault glows share their descriptor's audio (Failure & Trail). **Light itself is silent**: this system emits no noise into Attention's intake (noise is a tool property, PC-10).
